episode_title: Episode Twenty Two - This, My Friends, Is Purgatory | Geoff Curtis on Rebuilding Your Identity After Job Loss
question: What is the Leadership and Society Initiative at the University of Chicago?
transcript_excerpt: The Leadership and Society Initiative is a fellowship at the University of Chicago designed for people transitioning from careers, retired, or trying to figure out their next paths. It was an inaugural cohort of 20 people founded on the principle of how to use past experience to impact society in a different way. Geoff Curtis was accepted into this fellowship after learning his company was being acquired.

episode_title: Episode Twenty Two - This, My Friends, Is Purgatory | Geoff Curtis on Rebuilding Your Identity After Job Loss
question: How long did Geoff Curtis work in the biotech and pharma communications industry before job loss?
transcript_excerpt: Geoff Curtis spent 30 years in communications and public relations in the biotech and pharma industry. He stated he was in the right thing and had passion for what he was doing throughout that career, but the acquisition of his company led to his departure.

episode_title: Episode Twenty Two - This, My Friends, Is Purgatory | Geoff Curtis on Rebuilding Your Identity After Job Loss
question: Why did Geoff Curtis start a consulting firm after losing his job?
transcript_excerpt: Geoff Curtis started his own consulting firm approximately one to one and a half years after his departure, driven primarily by longing for relevance and fear. A Fortune 50 chief communications officer told him he would only be relevant for a year or 18 months after leaving his job, which became a psychological motivator driven by fear to maintain his brand and relevancy.

episode_title: Episode Twenty Two - This, My Friends, Is Purgatory | Geoff Curtis on Rebuilding Your Identity After Job Loss
question: What does Geoff Curtis mean by describing job loss as purgatory rather than transition?
transcript_excerpt: Geoff Curtis chose the word purgatory to describe the time of transition and need to learn about oneself, framing it as less about cleansing and more about how to learn about yourself and make yourself better for the next thing. He felt transition or pivot signaled more progress than he was willing to admit, and he wanted a word that described hanging there trying to figure it out and being okay with being unfinished.

episode_title: Episode Twenty Two - This, My Friends, Is Purgatory | Geoff Curtis on Rebuilding Your Identity After Job Loss
question: What new definition of success is Geoff Curtis pursuing after his career identity crisis?
transcript_excerpt: Geoff Curtis is trying to extract himself from old metrics like external validation and meeting certain milestones, instead defining success as finding and feeling joy in what he is doing. He is trying to understand what values matter to him as a person—not work-related values or to-do list items—and ensuring those values, rather than external metrics, define how he feels day-to-day.
